question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants citizens the right to freedom of speech and expression, freedom of assembly and freedom to practice any profession?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
 
• It guarantees the citizens of India the **right to freedom of speech and expression**.
 
• It also includes the **freedom to assemble peacefully without arms**.
 
• Additionally, it encompasses the **freedom to practice any profession** or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interests of **sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the state, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency, or morality**, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation, or incitement to an offense.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 17**__

 __
 
• Article 17 of the **Indian Constitution** abolishes **untouchability**.
 
• It forbids its practice in any form.
 
• The enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offense punishable in accordance with the law.
 
 
 
• **Article 18**__
 __
 
• **Article 18** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **abolition of titles**.
 
• It prohibits the state from conferring any titles, except military and academic distinctions.
 
• It also forbids Indian citizens from accepting any titles from a foreign state.
 
 
 
• **Article 25**__
 
 
• Article 25 of the **Indian Constitution** guarantees **freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion**.
 
• This freedom is subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• It also provides for the state to regulate or restrict any economic, financial, political, or other secular activity associated with religious practice.
